findings.note: Paragraph 2 says 'California law says junk, debris, garbage and pests make a building substandard.' This turns 'listed conditions that can make a building substandard' into a flat rule. The statute (clm:8 quote) makes a building substandard only when a listed condition exists 'to an extent that endangers the life, limb, health, property, safety, or welfare of the occupants of the building, nearby residents, or the public'. Pests are also listed only as infestation as determined by a health officer or code enforcement officer, and 'pests' and 'garbage' are not the statute's wording.

The unit cites clm:8, and clm:1, 2, 3 and 4 all carry their threshold in clm:8, but the unit never states the threshold anywhere (not in the paragraphs, the table or the note). The table rows read as if the condition alone is enough. The reader would believe a listed condition by itself makes a home substandard. State once, near the table, that a listed condition counts only 'to an extent that endangers the life, limb, health, property, safety, or welfare of the occupants of the building, nearby residents, or the public' (SR-5).

Table row 1 gives 'The local enforcement authority' as who decides, and the paragraph after the table says 'The local enforcement authority makes that call'. The stored quote for 17920.3(j) (clm:1) names no decider, and no ledger claim supports who decides for (j). Who decides is a legal claim and needs a claim or must go. The paragraph also presents one decider for all four rows, while rows 2 to 4 name a health officer, code enforcement officer or fire chief or deputy.

'Local rules differ by city and county' is close to, but not, the standing wording. SR-2 says to use 'local rules vary; check with your city or county' for an unverified local rule. The Oakland link is a real THB page and is kept as background, so only the wording changes.
